source.title: Tracing distinguishability through transformer processing with stochastic LayerNorm

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures distinguishability in GPT-2 attention projections and compares some selective heads with induction-related heads cited in prior work, but it does not test IOI behavior or the claimed circuit, its causal roles, or any of the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2 experiments use minimally perturbed noun-substitution pairs, not IOI prompts, and do not ablate or patch the claimed circuit. The paper cites prior IOI and induction-head analyses; those cited results are not results of this study. Its own head-selectivity results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GPT-2 small with stochastic LayerNorm reads and measures how much noun-substitution distinguishability each head's Q/K/V projections retain. It uses no IOI prompts, does no ablation or patching of the IOI circuit, and does not measure IOI behaviour. The IOI paper is cited only to name L5H5, L6H9 and L5H8 as induction or fuzzy-induction heads. The recorded relation 'discusses' overstates this; the text mentions the IOI paper only in passing.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present stochastic-read distinguishability as a functionally grounded complement to point-representation analyses and call the experiments a proof of concept. They say the head selectivity aligns with induction motifs but is only partly reflected in prefix-matching scores.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses stochastic LayerNorm fine-tuning and Bhattacharyya-overlap measurements of token-perturbation distinguishability, rather than IOI circuit discovery, ablation, or activation patching.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports head- and projection-specific selectivity, and says excess key selectivity for layer 5 heads decays with distance from the perturbed token. It does not test sensitivity of IOI circuit evaluation choices.

fits_no_version.finding: In stochastic-LayerNorm GPT-2 small, seven middle-layer heads' K projections retain more noun-swap distinguishability than random 64-dimensional projections. Six of the seven are linked to induction, including L5H5, L6H9 and L5H8, which the IOI paper labels as induction heads. In most of these heads Q and V stay near the random baseline; L4H7 is high on Q, K and V.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-related GPT-2 heads selectively expose token-perturbation distinctions through their key projections.

record.problems: The GPT-2 head-selectivity results are presented qualitatively without numerical retained fractions in the text; the authors note that their local-posterior approximation and treatment of upstream stochasticity are limited, and that conclusions from rate-limited models may not transfer to unconstrained models.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Vision augmentation measurements and general stochasticity analyses were not extracted because they do not bear on the IOI circuit claim.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.stage_stated: pretrained model fine-tuned with stochastic LayerNorm reads
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of upstream Bhattacharyya distance preserved by each attention key projection for minimally perturbed noun-substitution pairs.

conditions.value: 80 minimally perturbed pairs; noun swaps retained at no more than 50 nats of Bhattacharyya distance at the layer 5 attention read after the perturbation

rows.measure: Fraction of upstream Bhattacharyya distance retained in K projections.
rows.baseline: Random 64-dimensional projections preserve around 0.1 of the upstream Bhattacharyya distance.
rows.value: Seven middle-layer heads stand out above the random-projection baseline; five coincide with high-induction-score heads. The text also identifies L5H8, L5H5, and L6H9 in relation to prior induction-head analyses, and says six of the seven selective heads have an independently observed induction connection.
rows.uncertainty: The figure shows a 5–95% spread for random projections; no numeric uncertainty for the learned-head results is stated.
rows.note: The text does not give numerical retained fractions for the learned heads. These are K-selectivity findings on noun substitutions, not measurements of IOI circuit roles.
rows.check: K-selectivity on noun swaps does not measure IOI circuit roles. The link to induction heads named in the IOI paper is a cited result, not this study's test of it.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.stage_stated: pretrained model fine-tuned with stochastic LayerNorm reads
rows.operation_detail: Compared query-projection distinguishability with key-projection selectivity for the highlighted heads.
rows.measure: Fraction of upstream Bhattacharyya distance retained in Q projections, compared with K projections.
rows.baseline: Random-projection baseline; its approximate value is stated for random 64-dimensional projections.
rows.value: Q projections remain near the random-projection baseline, unlike the highlighted heads' K projections.
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative; no Q-projection fractions are stated.
rows.check: 'Partial' has no meaning against any claim version. The row records Q projections staying near the random baseline, a head-selectivity finding unrelated to IOI.
